objective: Determine whether the existing Wingless substrate can learn directly from raw byte streams while developing compact reusable multiscale internal representations that reduce effective computation and preserve or improve generalization relative to fixed-granularity baselines.
substrate_preservation: This proposal tests granularity inside the existing Wingless substrate. It does not authorize replacing the substrate with a conventional transformer, tokenizer-first model, or external frontier model.
research_claim_to_test: Raw bytes can remain the universal input granularity while Wingless learns higher internal granularities only where they improve prediction, reuse, generalization, or compute efficiency.
candidate_input_granularities: bit-level raw stream as a small-scale stress-test extreme
fixed byte-only processing with no learned aggregation
fixed character or fixed subword segmentation as comparison baselines only

proposed_test_ladder.name: raw-byte acquisition baseline
proposed_test_ladder.question: Can the native substrate learn predictive structure directly from bytes without a tokenizer?
proposed_test_ladder.design: Train on a frozen synthetic byte language with deterministic train/validation/test splits. Compare byte-native Wingless against an information-matched fixed-symbol baseline under preregistered state and compute budgets.
proposed_test_ladder.gate: Byte-native learning must exceed an untrained baseline and remain deterministic/reproducible before adaptive aggregation is introduced.

proposed_test_ladder.name: emergent multi-byte motif formation
proposed_test_ladder.question: Can the substrate discover reusable multi-byte units without a supplied lexicon or tokenizer?
proposed_test_ladder.design: Expose repeated and compositional byte motifs while allowing only bounded internal aggregation. Compare against byte-only and static-chunk controls.
primary_metrics: held-out predictive gain attributable to learned motifs
active-compute reduction at matched predictive quality
false motif formation on frequency-matched random controls
proposed_test_ladder.gate: A learned motif counts only if causal ablation degrades held-out prediction or efficiency and a matched random/shuffled control does not reproduce the benefit.

proposed_test_ladder.name: adaptive granularity under uncertainty
proposed_test_ladder.question: Can Wingless spend byte-level compute on surprising regions while using coarser learned representations on predictable regions?
proposed_test_ladder.design: Freeze mixed low-entropy/high-entropy byte streams and compare fixed byte, static chunk, and entropy-adaptive internal granularity at matched quality targets.
primary_metrics: compute per byte by entropy stratum
proposed_test_ladder.gate: Adaptive granularity must reduce compute at matched quality without hidden capacity growth or oracle boundary labels.

proposed_test_ladder.name: cross-domain granularity transfer
proposed_test_ladder.question: Do learned byte-level structures transfer across prose-like, code-like, structured-data, and binary-like synthetic domains?
proposed_test_ladder.design: Use preregistered disjoint domains with common low-level motifs and domain-specific higher structure. Measure reuse versus unnecessary specialization.
proposed_test_ladder.gate: Transfer must be demonstrated on sealed held-out domains; post-result motif relabeling or boundary tuning is forbidden.

proposed_test_ladder.name: multiscale native-language precursor
proposed_test_ladder.question: Can raw bytes support a hierarchy from byte motifs to larger reusable sequence structures without an external tokenizer?
proposed_test_ladder.design: Scale the best qualified granularity mechanism to a controlled language-like corpus with morphology, syntax-like dependencies, and long-range references.
proposed_test_ladder.gate: This remains a controlled precursor and does not count as open-domain language competence.

required_controls: static chunking with equal or lower representational capacity
fixed-token/subword baseline only as an external scientific comparator, never as the deployed substrate
success_definition: Evidence for a substrate advantage requires matched or better held-out predictive/generalization quality with materially lower effective compute, shorter internal sequence length, stronger transfer, or lower persistent state growth than fixed-granularity controls. Interesting-looking chunks without causal/efficiency evidence are not success.
failure_definition: The hypothesis is weakened if learned granularity adds complexity without quality/compute benefit, collapses under OOD transfer, requires hand-authored boundaries, or merely recreates a static tokenizer with no measurable substrate advantage.
sequencing_rule: Do not interrupt or mutate a currently frozen experiment. Promote one stage at a time into a separate preregistration only after its prerequisites are satisfied. Freeze seeds, splits, budgets, controls, metrics, thresholds, and stop rules before implementation.
authority: proposal only; no execution, scheduler, queue-consumer, accepted-ref, deployment, runtime, broker, or external-model inference authority
